title: Prove: Queue-based load leveling trades latency for stability
body:
Inserting a queue between producers and consumers smooths bursty demand and protects downstream services, at the cost of added latency, backlog, and operational complexity.

Complexity: Admission and dequeue are O(1) amortized per item; end-to-end latency includes queue wait time proportional to backlog and service time.

title: Invariant: Queue-based load leveling trades latency for stability
body: The queue decouples arrival rate from processing rate: accepted work is durable until a consumer processes it, so overload becomes backlog rather than immediate failure.

title: Proof step: Absorb bursts at the boundary
body: Producers append work items to a buffer instead of calling the downstream service synchronously; amortized-constant append keeps admission cheap under bursts.

title: Proof step: Consumers process at a steady rate
body:
Workers dequeue from the front at a controlled pace; constant-time front removal supports steady drain without re-scanning buffered work.

Depends on: enqueue

title: Proof step: Backpressure becomes queue depth
body:
When arrivals exceed service rate, latency grows with depth and unbounded queues risk memory/time exhaustion; bounds, TTLs, or dead-lettering make the trade-off explicit.

Depends on: enqueue, drain

title: Proof step: Reliability gained, simplicity lost
body:
The design improves resilience and elasticity but introduces eventual processing, ordering/idempotency concerns, monitoring of lag, and extra infrastructure to operate.

Depends on: backlog
